narrative:
The model determined that you have a 54% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and your property ownership. Your credit history had the greatest impact and pushed the decision toward denial. Having no credits or all paid puts you in a very small group—only 1% of approved applicants share this profile—making the model view your repayment reliability as uncertain. Next, the status of your checking account also increased the risk score. Your balance in the 0-200 DM range is less favorable than the none or higher-balance accounts that most approved applicants have. Finally, owning real estate worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval, as this is generally seen as a positive sign of stability. However, it was not enough to overcome the concerns from the first two factors.

Your relatively short loan duration, lower requested amount, and younger age played only minor roles. 

To improve your chances on future applications, focus on building a longer, positive credit history with this bank, aim to keep a stronger checking account balance, and consider reapplying once those areas show clear improvement.
